name: vv-hero
claim: Every frame, a function of n.

graphicEarnsIt.says: The shape of an easing curve sampled once per frame. Eighteen bars, one for each frame n = 0 to n = 17, and each bar's height is that frame's output value. You can read the motion off it directly: a near-zero first bar, three or four fast-growing bars, then a long flat tail where every value is pinned at 1.00. That is the curve's story, most of the distance covered early and the end crawling in. Beat 1 shows the same series as literal numbers (.00 .33 .56 .71 .80 ... 1.00 1.00) and beat 2 redraws those numbers as length, so the graphic and the headline say the same thing in two languages. The thin vertical rule is the playhead, marking which n the film itself is sitting on, which makes the chart a picture of the very frame you are watching.

One bar per animation frame, n = 0 to 17, bar height = the eased value at that frame (0 up to 1). The steep early rise and long flat tail read as an ease-out curve, and the vertical rule is the playhead showing which frame is on screen right now. In beat 1 the same series is shown as its raw numbers (.00 .33 .56 .71 .80 .87 ... 1.00) before it becomes bars in beat 2, so the pair reads as numbers turning into motion. LEFT encodes nothing; its soft oval vignette is decoration.

An easing curve sampled per frame: 18 frame indices (n = 0 to 17) each carrying a value from 0.00 to 1.00, shown first as the literal numbers and then as bar heights, with a vertical playhead marking the current frame. You can read the shape of easeOutExpo straight off it, fast rise then a long flatten into 1.00, so the picture shows what 'every frame is a function of n' actually means. LEFT has no picture at all: a soft radial wash behind the type, which is decoration.

perBeat.why: Same headline both sides, but RIGHT backs the words with a real readout (a row of eased values from .00 to 1.00 across n = 0..17 with a playhead on the current frame) while LEFT is the sentence alone on empty white.
RIGHT turns the claim into a picture, a bar per frame whose height is the eased value, so the bottom half of the canvas does work; LEFT leaves the same half of the frame blank.
